lawyer:
Monindra Biswas ----- Plaintiffs-Respondents-Petitioners
vs
Khalilur Rahman Chowdhury ----- Defendant-Appellant-Opposite Party
parties:
Md Zakir Hossain with Abdul Jalil, Advocates — For the Petitioners. 

AKM Badrudduza, Advocate — For the Opposite Party.
full_judgment: 9. Learned Advocate Mr AKM Badrudduza appeared for the defendant-appellant-opposite party. He, at the very outset, points out that there is only one schedule in the disputed deed No.2347 dated 15-2-1999 (Exhibit Kha = Exhibit-1 of the defendant). But in the plaint, the plaintiffs have given two different schedules. He next submits that, in the schedule to the disputed deed, both the PS Plots No.1406 and No. 1410 have been specifically mentioned, out of which 0.1750 acres of land was sold to the defendant and possession has been given in 0.1750 acres of land of PS Plot No.1406, since that was intended to be purchased by the defendant-buyer and was sold to him and that, the defendant is in peaceful and continuous possession of the purchased land by erecting boundary wall and other demarcation. He next submits that, in the report of the Advocate Commissioner, both the PS Plot Nos.1406 and 1410 have been marked with green colour as the disputed land, while the Advocate Commissioner has also marked PS Plot No. 1413 in green colour as the disputed property, which is not in the schedule to the disputed deed. He next submits that, the Advocate Commissioner's report is not correct, rather it is misleading, and reliance on the said report by the trial court was not proper. He proceeds on that, the defendant is the bonafide purchaser for value and, in fact, the plaintiffs have no title in PS Plot No. 1410, which was acquired by the Government and the plaintiffs has handed over possession of 0.1740 acres of land from PS Plot No. 1406 and the defendant-purchaser is still possessing the same. He further submits that, there is no consistency between the prayer portion of the plaint and the schedule of the plaint and that, there is no evidence on record to prove any case of fraud as alleged. He next submits that, exhibit-3, which is claimed to be mutation khatian of the defendant, is an unsigned document and the same was not admissible in evidence. Hence, the trial court should not have marked the said khatian as exhibit No. 3 and the trial court should not have relied upon exhibit-3 to arrive at the finding in passing the judgment and decree in favour of the plaintiff. As regards the judgment of the appellate court, the learned Advocate submits that, the defendant filed Title Suit No. 419 of 2008 for rectification of the sale deed No.2347 dated 15-2-1999 (Exhibit Kha = Exhibit-1) by deleting PS Plot No. 1410 from the said deed, therefore, in order to avoid a conflicting judgments and having found that the judgment of the trial court was not proper, the appellate court has rightly set-aside the judgment of the trial court and that tantamounts to reversal of the findings of the trial court and, therefore, had sent the suit on remand for fresh trial of Title Suit No. 85 of 2005 along with Title Suit No. 419 of 2008, so that the case and evidences of both the parties can be considered together and a proper judgment can be passed. He also submits that, the appellate court is competent to send the Title Suit 85 of 2005 on remand and in passing the judgment and decree of the trial court; the appellate court has committed no error of law causing any prejudice to the parties. He, therefore, submits that, this Rule has no merit and the same may kindly be discharged.
